# Appeal of Denial – Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Skyler Ellison
**Member ID:** W240749705
**Reference Number:** POC-1C51E72E1E-65750
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-24
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery, https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/

Dear PacificSource Appeals Team,

I am writing to formally request reconsideration of the denial of coverage for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030), which was denied on 2026-08-24 for "incomplete documentation." My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in your file meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## The records show I completed the required conservative management

The plan's policy states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

The records establish that I completed supervised physical therapy — 24 visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. In addition to physical therapy, I completed more than one complementary treatment strategy. The policy lists acceptable complementary strategies as including:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Epidural corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

My records show I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. Both of these are named in the plan's own list of qualifying complementary treatments.

## The records show conservative management failed

The plan's policy states that:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following:"

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My records document that I completed a full 10-week course of physical therapy plus medication and injection treatment, and that despite this, I still cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and continue to have radicular pain into my right calf. My MRI from 2026-07-28 and physical exam, showing positive provocative testing and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, were obtained after this conservative treatment concluded, showing that my symptoms did not resolve. Surgery is now the treatment being considered by my surgeon. This matches each element the plan requires to establish failure of conservative management.

## The records document a neurologic deficit from nerve compression

The plan's policy also states that conservative management is not always a prerequisite:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when myelopathy, weakness, or bladder disturbance is present."

My MRI of 2026-07-28 documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root, and my exam shows a neurologic deficit corresponding to that imaged level. This finding independently supports the medical necessity of surgery under the plan's own guideline, in addition to the conservative management history described above.

## Functional impact

The plan states that:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes and have ongoing radicular pain into my right calf. [Placeholder: specific numeric pain rating, if documented in the chart, to be inserted here] I ask that the plan review the full chart for any additional documentation of pain severity and functional limitation that may not have been included in the original submission.

## Request

Based on the plan's own criteria, compared against my documented conservative treatment history, imaging findings, and exam findings, I am asking PacificSource to reverse this denial and approve coverage for CPT 63030. If any specific document is still considered missing from my file, I would appreciate a clear list of exactly what is needed so that my surgeon's office and I can supply it promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-20. I am submitting it as follows: [Placeholder: submission method selected — e.g., electronic submission via InTouch "Ask a Question," email to NewAppeal@PacificSource.com, fax to 541-225-3628, or mail to the appeal address printed on the denial letter]. I understand I may also call 888-977-9299 (TTY 711) with questions about this appeal.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

________________________
Skyler Ellison
Member ID: W240749705
Date: [Placeholder: date of signature]
Contact phone/email: [Placeholder]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
